title: The Shadow City
subtitle: A seven-dimensional metropolis
story:
The storm has you. No matter how you bank, it will not let go, and it carries you round and round the city at its heart. And the city is wrong. It is deeper than the space it stands in, seven dimensions deep, and from out here you only ever see its shadows. From most angles, you see it as a heap of towers growing through one another. But by looking from the right headings, maybe it might make sense...

Your orders: sample the cloud-gardens drifting through the storm to chart the city, then find the two headings at which the city's properties align and follow them. That is the only way out.

done.title: The survey is charted
done.body: Both of the city's great shadows lie charted on the console. Out in the eyewall the lightning stutters and stops, and on your dash the six dark cells around the override begin, faintly, to glow. Somewhere on the ring, over the city's heart, the cloud has parted.

escapeDone.title: Out of the storm
escapeDone.body: The six cells settle and hold. You pull the release, and the glider climbs the calm column of light: the eyewall falls away beneath you like the walls of a well, the city shrinks to a bright, many-coloured star at its bottom, and then there is only open sky.

Strong simple shapes that read at thumbnail size. No people, no text, no lettering.

debrief.title: How this world worked
debrief.intro: The whole flight was one act of principal-components analysis, made into a place. Your cloud-garden samples measured seven properties, so each bloom was a point in seven dimensions, and so was the city: far too many dimensions to see at once. What reached you from any heading was only a shadow, a projection of those seven dimensions down to what an eye can take in. From most headings the shadow was a heap. PCA finds the few directions along which that shadow spreads out the most, the principal components, and tells you what each one is made of, its loadings. You worked the numbers at the console, then flew the ring to find those directions by eye. The trap was believing the biggest shadow shows you everything.

out past the left wing, INBOARD, across open air in the MIDDLE DISTANCE and spread wide across the whole left side of the view, the city seen WHOLE along this heading: the city is not of our world: ONE vast shared volume of open sky filled with a sprawling, FLOATING city made of EXACTLY SEVEN KINDS of building, each clearly distinct, every kind scattered right through the same volume and INTERMIXED with all the others. Each kind is its own city with its own direction of 'up'. NOTHING in this city stands upright: every building leans, lies sideways, hangs upside down or juts out on a diagonal, at ALL ANGLES to its neighbours, and buildings run straight THROUGH one another where they cross. Some buildings are only HALF THERE — ghostly and semi-transparent, the storm and other buildings showing through them — while others are fully solid with crisp, HARD outlines, and some fade from solid at one end to translucent at the other. (1) FILAMENT: slender towers spun from bundled glowing threads, like fibre-optic crystal, light running up their strands. (2) NECTAR: translucent honeycomb halls and hives, lit warm amber-gold from inside. (3) ACID: etched, pitted towers of pale acid-green crystal, as if eaten into, glowing faintly. (4) PIGMENT: buildings of pure stained glass in fully saturated jewel colours, blazing ruby, cobalt and violet. (5) SPORE: clustered domes and round pods of smoky black shadow, soft-edged, no detail at all — a SHADOW kind. (6) DRIFT: paper-thin flat black silhouettes of buildings, perfectly two-dimensional cut-outs that vanish to a hairline where seen edge-on — a SHADOW kind. (7) MOISTURE: towers of black mirror like still water or obsidian, reflecting the storm and the other buildings — a SHADOW kind. Kinds 1-4 glow in colour; kinds 5-7 are three DIFFERENT sorts of shadow. Colossal: buildings kilometres tall seen from far off, so NO staircases, steps, windows, railings or doorways are visible; it floats with NOTHING beneath it. Among the buildings drift CLOUD-GARDENS: pale, softly GLOWING drifts of living mist — luminous spore-clouds with a faint inner light, white, pearl and pale grey, some nearly transparent; never jellyfish, never plain cumulus, never coloured. Each building kind keeps its own colour identity — THE COLOUR BELONGS TO THE CITY (Lucas, 2026-09-21). No nets, webs or cables strung between buildings. From HERE its shadow is this: a HEAP: every district collapsed onto every other — all seven kinds tilted AGAINST each other at clashing angles and crammed into the same space, dozens of buildings passing straight THROUGH each other, a dense impossible tangle with no common 'up' anywhere, with no line or order to it; just beyond the left wingtip, a slack back-eddy in the current peels away and curls the other way round the ring

The sleeping override was the promise that reading the city was the way out.

rooms.debrief: The escape was the technique with the numbers stripped away. You could only reach the Eye, the city's centre, by flying in along one of its two principal headings, just as PCA measures its axes from the centre of the data. The panel then asked you to reconstruct which of the towers' traits rise together, which run against each other and which are unrelated, read off the two shadows you had flown. That is reading a biplot: the correlation structure a PCA is built from.
